subject: MSA + Order Form: derivative rights, feedback license, and escrow path
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@brightline.ai>
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: Legal Ops <legalops@brightline.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@procurecorp.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood MSA / Order Form – initial redline requests

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday — Brightline is excited to move forward. Legal had a quick pass and surfaced three principal concerns we want to address before we proceed to signature:

1) Output ownership / attribution: we prefer a clause that grants Brightline ownership of outputs produced using their confidential prompts/data;
2) Training / model reuse: we cannot consent to broad training/use of our data unless there is an explicit opt-in and documented controls;
3) Feedback license: Legal prefers a limited, non-exclusive license for telemetry/feedback data for product improvements that excludes model retraining on customer data without explicit opt-in.

I attached their redline snapshot and a short summary (see attachments). Can Redwood provide proposed language that narrows training consent, offers an escrow or split for derivative rights, and a clear feedback license carve-out?

We’re hoping to get this to procurement by next week.

Best,
Elena
Elena Ruiz
VP, Legal 
Brightline AI

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the clear summary. I’m looping in our legal and product owners to converge on proposed language. High-level plan:

- Internal sync today (legal + product) to draft alternative clauses that limit training to anonymized/aggregated telemetry and require explicit customer opt-in for retraining.
- Propose a narrow feedback license (timebound, non-exclusive) that excludes derivative model ownership.
- For output ownership, we can offer a customer ownership statement for outputs but retain model IP and a carve-out for aggregated improvements. If Brightline needs a stronger guarantee we can propose an escrow-like arrangement for certain model artifacts (more on feasibility after legal review).

I’ll send a redline back with tracked language by Monday EOD PST. If Brightline has preferred clause examples, please share.

Thanks —

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: camila_reyes@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: MSA redline draft guidance (Brightline)

Team —

I reviewed Brightline’s requested changes. Below are recommended positions for the external-facing redline (keeps negotiations tight but commercially reasonable):

1) Output ownership: Agree to customer ownership of "Customer Outputs" defined as content produced in response to Customer Input that is not derived from Redwood proprietary models or datasets. Add explicit exclusion: "Customer Outputs do not include Model Weights, training datasets, or model architectures."

2) Training / retraining: Reject permissive unilateral training rights. Propose: "Redwood will not use Customer Input or Customer Outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve models used for Customer’s account without Customer's prior written opt-in. Redwood may use aggregated and de-identified telemetry solely for service performance diagnostics and model quality metrics."

3) Feedback license: Offer a limited, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use feedback (comments on model performance) for product improvements, but explicitly exclude using Feedback as Training Data for customer-profiled models unless the customer opts in via the Order Form.

4) Escrow / derivative rights: Escrow for model artifacts is complex operationally. Offer a middle-ground: an audit right and a documented export capability of Customer Outputs upon termination. If customer insists on escrow of model binaries, escalate to Sales + Ops for SOW and pricing.

I’ve drafted alternative language in the attached doc (redlines_camila_v1.docx). Laura — please chime in on compliance/audit language and whether we can commit to export tooling within 60 days of go-live.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: internal: MSA redline draft guidance (Brightline)

Agree with Karthik’s positions. Couple of execution notes:

- Compliance/audit: We can commit to a quarterly attestation of telemetry handling and provide a SOC-type summary for how customer data is segregated. Not comfortable promising a 60-day export for all customers — propose 90 days for first release and then 60 days as part of a roadmap commitment.
- Escrow: Operational cost needs to be communicated. If they ask for escrow of model binaries or weights we should price it as an add-on.
- Feedback license: Add a clause that feedback excludes PII and that Redwood will follow a documented redaction process prior to any use in research pipelines.

Marcus — can you confirm there’s no technical blocker to providing export of Customer Outputs as described? Also, how long would it take to provide an automated export tool (zip + manifest) we could offer as standard for enterprise customers?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: internal: MSA redline draft guidance (Brightline)

Laura — quick technical note:

We can implement a Customer Output export (ZIP + manifest) and an export API. Estimating 8-10 weeks for an initial automated self-serve export (depends on priority and QA). Manual exports by ops are possible within 5 business days today at no technical barrier.

On telemetry redaction: we have hooks to strip user identifiers; I’ll work with Trust to formalize the redaction checklist for the legal clause.

I’ll review the drafted language and flag anything technically infeasible. Once legal finalizes wording, we can include an implementation timeline in the Order Form (e.g., "Export tooling will be available within 90 days of contract execution unless otherwise agreed").

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 7 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA / Order Form – initial redline requests

Elena —

Thanks for the patience. Attached is a proposed redline set that addresses Brightline’s three priority items: ownership of Customer Outputs (narrowed definition), explicit opt-in for any retraining using Customer data, and a limited feedback license that excludes training unless opted-in on the Order Form. We also included a proposed implementation timeline for an automated export tool (90 days) and an operations fallback (manual export within 5 business days).

Key changes summarized:
- Customer Outputs: explicit customer ownership, with carve-outs for model weights/architectures and for aggregated improvements.
- Training: no use of Customer Input/Outputs for model training without prior written opt-in; allowed use of de-identified telemetry for diagnostics.
- Feedback License: perpetual, non-exclusive license for product improvement excluding Training Data for customer-specific models. Feedback will be redacted to remove PII prior to use.

If this looks acceptable I can circulate the redlined MSA + Order Form to Brightline Legal and propose a 30-minute call to walk through the language and confirm the export timeline.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Senior AM, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
